text:
Athena has no queue triage step; the operator closes done or superseded requests by hand

A person approved this proposal from the steward role. Carry the work out as an ordinary change.
Everything the proposal cites is copied below; nothing here points at a file you cannot open.

Proposal: 20261027-044222-febw (key queue-triage-done-by-operator-by-hand), queued at 2026-10-27T04:42:22.19966158Z by the steward role.

Athena's plan refused that request because it lacked acceptance criteria, and it put stale work first. Under OP-17 the operator did the triage by hand. They closed 17 queue items with reasons (done, stale, superseded or merged). They kept one item, read-only git history for agents, against the triage's advice. No job ran and no job failed.",
  "failure_class": "20261017-182445-0592",

  "cause": "Athena treats every request as a deliverable job with checkable acceptance criteria. Queue maintenance is judgment over existing items, and its outcome (each item has a disposition and a reason) is not something the planner can state as acceptance. Nothing lets a request that acts on the queue define its own criteria. Plan ordering also does not check whether an item is stale before putting it first. So a decision the owner had already made could not run through Athena, and the operator had to do it.",
  "prevention_kind": "design-change",
  "prevention": "Add a queue-triage work type with built-in acceptance. Every open item gets a disposition (keep, done, stale, superseded or merged) with a reason checked against the current brief and main. Closing items is allowed, and an item kept against the advice needs an explicit owner override. Plan ordering must skip or revalidate items marked stale. Admission would then not refuse a triage request for lacking acceptance, and the operator would only review the proposed dispositions.",
  "proposed_request": "Re-triage every open item in the Athena queue against the Olympus brief and the current main branch. For each item, record one disposition: keep, done, stale, superseded or merged. Give a one-line reason that cites evidence, such as a merged commit or a brief section. Close the items that are not kept, and leave the kept ones in the queue. Report the dispositions in a table for the owner to review. Acceptance: no open item lacks a disposition and reason. Every closed item names the evidence for closing it. Any keep that goes against the triage's advice is listed separately for the owner to confirm. Do not start work on any kept item.",

  "cause": "Athena has no triage capability for its own queue. Nothing re-checks whether queued requests are still wanted, done or superseded, and the requirements engineer role that would own this judgment does not exist yet. Queue grooming therefore falls to the operator by default.",
  "prevention_kind": "design-change",
  "prevention": "Add a triage stage or role, the requirements engineer. It would review open queued requests against landed work and current state. For each request it would propose keep, close-as-done or close-as-superseded, with a recorded reason. Closures would run through the normal lifecycle commands and be logged. Triage would have a defined acceptance shape so it can be requested and verified like any other job.",
  "proposed_request": "Add a queue triage capability to Athena. Outcome: when asked, Athena reviews every open queued request against landed jobs and the current repo state. It classifies each as still needed, already done, or superseded, and gives a one-line reason citing the evidence, such as the landing job id. Requests judged done or superseded are closed through the normal close command with that reason recorded. Requests that are still needed stay untouched. Anything uncertain is listed for the owner and not closed. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fixture queue holding one done, one superseded and one live request shows the first two closed with reasons and the live one kept; (2) every closure is logged as an Athena action, not an unlogged operator intervention; (3) the report lists kept, closed and uncertain items with reasons; (4) running it twice changes nothing the second time.",
